display.purpose: The HedgeGuesser name only, as neon tubes.

headline.purpose: Screen headings and the OUT OF ORDER sign.

label.purpose: Text printed on arcade caps, stage duration labels, dim section headings.

plate.purpose: Small uppercase labels naming a control, readout or section; never a kicker.

score.purpose: Amber score digits over an amber-off ghost.

shadows.name: shadow-panel
shadows.purpose: Things that sit on the cabinet: panels, strips, lists, marquee board.

shadows.name: shadow-housing
shadows.purpose: The black collar around every arcade button.

shadows.name: pink-glow
shadows.purpose: Lit pink caps, selected strips, lit pips.

shadows.name: cyan-glow
shadows.purpose: Current stage segment, meter, marquee outline tube.

shadows.name: red-glow
shadows.purpose: Life pips, miss ticks, red caps.

shadows.name: pink-glow-text
shadows.purpose: Lit lettering only: marquee tubes, panel titles. Never body copy.

shadows.name: recess
shadows.purpose: Things set into the cabinet: input slots, tracks, pip strips.

motion.name: ease-press
motion.purpose: Cap release with a little spring; presses snap down in 40ms.

motion.name: marquee-flicker
motion.purpose: Irregular tube stutter that always ends lit; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition 0.01ms, one iteration; [data-decor] and .confetti display: none
motion.purpose: Everything collapses to its lit, at-rest frame.

narrative.northStar: The Cabinet with a Jukebox Inside
narrative.overview:
HedgeGuesser is one physical machine the player stands in front of. It is not a dark web page with glowing card borders. Every surface is a part of a coin-op cabinet: violet side-art panels, black plastic bezels, recessed LCD and CRT windows, concave arcade caps that drop into their collars, LED pips, and jukebox title strips with selection codes. Light is the material. A thing glows only when it is lit, and it is lit only when it is live or interactive.

Density is low and the column is narrow (720px max), one cabinet face, centred. The type does three jobs with three voices: neon-tube lettering for the name, painted sign lettering for controls and headings, and a condensed sans for reading. Score is the fourth voice: amber seven-segment digits over their own unlit ghost.

Motion is physical and short (120 to 600ms): presses, roll-ups, flickers, a single marquee flash. Under reduced motion every animation collapses to its lit, at-rest frame and decorative particles are removed.
keyCharacteristics: Ground is cabinet-night (#0f051d), with a faint violet radial wash from the top and a whole-screen scanline veil at no more than 3.5% white.
Colour has jobs: pink for player action, cyan for audio and progress, amber for points, red for misses, lives and destruction.
Every role colour ships as a set of four: base, highlight, shade, and unlit. Off states show the unlit tube, never a grey.
Depth is physical: offset-and-blur shadows under things that sit on the cabinet, inset shadows for things set into it.
Self-hosted fonts only; no third-party font hosts.

rules.name: The Colour Has Jobs Rule
rules.body: Pink acts, cyan plays, amber scores, red misses. Never use a role colour for decoration or for a job that belongs to another. A new surface that needs emphasis picks the role whose job it is, or stays neutral.

rules.name: The Unlit Tube Rule
rules.body: An off, locked, or disabled thing shows its role's unlit tone (the `-off` value) or a violet neutral, never grey and never a reduced-opacity copy of the lit colour. A disabled control reads as a lamp that is out.

rules.name: The Lit Means Live Rule
rules.body: Glow (`--*-glow`, `--*-glow-text`) belongs only to lit, interactive or live elements: caps, current segments, pips that are on, the marquee, the score. Body copy and static panels never glow.

rules.name: The Marquee Is the Name Rule
rules.body: Monoton sets the word HedgeGuesser and nothing else.

rules.name: The Instrument Label Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase Bungee plates name a control, a readout or a section. They never sit above a larger heading as a tagline or kicker.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every counter, score, time and table number uses `tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Sits-On or Set-In Rule
rules.body: Every surface either sits on the cabinet (drop shadow) or is set into it (inset). Pick one; do not float a card with a soft ambient shadow.

rules.name: The One Tube Rule
rules.body: The scanline veil covers the whole screen, overlays included, so the screen reads as one tube. It never blocks input and never drops text contrast.

dos: **Do** pick a role colour by its job: pink for actions, cyan for audio and progress, amber for points, red for misses and destruction.
**Do** show off states with the role's `-off` tone or a violet neutral, so a disabled control reads as an unlit lamp.
**Do** use the neutral ArcadeButton for navigation and utility keys, and reserve lit caps for the actions that matter on that screen.
**Do** keep motion between 120ms and 600ms on `--ease-out` and `--ease-press`. Collapse every animation to its lit final frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and remove `[data-decor]` and confetti.
**Do** keep text at least 44px tap-tall in controls, and keep the score and counters tabular.
**Do** make every surface either sit on the cabinet (panel or housing shadow) or be set into it (inset).
donts: **Don't** set anything but the name in Monoton.
**Don't** glow body copy or static panels; glow is for lit and live things only.
**Don't** use grey for disabled states, and don't fade a lit colour with opacity to mean off.
**Don't** let any veil or scanline lower text contrast or intercept input.
**Don't** put a small uppercase plate above a heading as a kicker; plates label instruments and sections only.
**Don't** load fonts from third-party hosts; every face is self-hosted and bundled.
